# LightRAG Storage Options — Technical Report

**Report status: PARTIAL**  
The research execution ended `partial_or_incomplete`: step 1 completed; steps 2 and 3 hit tool-round limits (partial); step 4 was blocked and never ran. This report synthesizes the evidence actually collected, labels each claim, and discloses exactly what remains unverified. It does **not** imply the research is complete.

---

## 1. Official documentation and repository

| Item | Finding | Evidence |
|------|---------|----------|
| Official documentation URL | `https://lightrag.github.io/` — reachable (HTTP 200, `text/html`); page title "LightRAG", description "LightRAG: Simple and Fast Retrieval-Augmented Generation" | [call-04181898](https://lightrag.github.io/), [call-966efac9](https://lightrag.github.io/) |
| Official GitHub repository | `https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag` (HKUDS/LightRAG) | [call-0e1ecf21](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag), [call-e9f41fad](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag) |
| Repository metadata | MIT license; ~40.5k stars; ~5.7k forks; 10,873 commits; associated with EMNLP2025 paper arXiv:2410.05779 | [call-aa2fac7a](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag), [call-b41807d6](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/hkuds/lightrag/main/README.md) |

**Assessment:** Claims `step_1:claim_1`, `step_1:claim_2`, and `step_1:claim_3` are **supported** by official sources.

---

## 2. Supported storage backends (evidence status: partial)

LightRAG defines four storage roles. The following is drawn from step-2 evidence citing `docs/ProgramingWithCore.md` and `docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md`. Because step 2 hit its tool-round limit, **claim `step_2:claim_5` (each backend claim cross-checked against official documentation) is unsupported**; treat the backend list as **partially supported**.

| Storage role | Purpose (per docs) | Default (demo/dev only) | Production-capable unified backends | Specialized / role-specific backends |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `KV_STORAGE` | LLM response cache, text chunks, document information | In-memory / file-persisted | PostgreSQL (`PGKVStorage`), MongoDB, OpenSearch | — |
| `VECTOR_STORAGE` | Entity, relation, and chunk embedding vectors | In-memory / file-persisted | PostgreSQL (`PGVectorStorage`) | Milvus, Qdrant |
| `GRAPH_STORAGE` | Entity–relation graph | In-memory / file-persisted | PostgreSQL (`PGGraphStorage`, via Apache AGE) | Neo4j, Memgraph |
| `DOC_STATUS_STORAGE` | Document indexing status | In-memory / file-persisted | PostgreSQL, MongoDB, OpenSearch | — |

Sources: [call-faa610e5](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md), [call-50201106](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md), [call-1fc3d299](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/ProgramingWithCore.md), [call-efcb1bae](https://www.prompts.brightcoding.dev/blog/lightrag-the-revolutionary-dual-level-graph-rag-system), [call-ff664c6a](https://github.com/hkuds/lightrag).

**Key documented caveat:** the default in-memory/file-persisted stores are suitable only for small-scale testing and evaluation, **not** production [call-1fc3d299].

---

## 3. Differences between the available storage options

This section is **reasoned synthesis** from the evidence above, not a direct quote from docs.

| Dimension | In-memory / file (default) | Unified backend (PostgreSQL / MongoDB / OpenSearch) | Specialized backends (Milvus/Qdrant, Neo4j/Memgraph) |
|---|---|---|---|
| Scope | All four roles in one lightweight store | All four roles in one operational database | One role only (vector or graph) |
| Query model | Simple key/value lookups | SQL (PostgreSQL) or document/query language | Vector similarity (Milvus/Qdrant); Cypher (Neo4j/Memgraph) |
| Durability / backup | Limited (file-persisted only) | Production-grade backup, replication, ACID (PostgreSQL) | Varies by product; separate operational footprint |
| Operational overhead | None | Single database to operate | Multiple databases to operate and keep in sync |
| Production suitability | No | Yes — PostgreSQL explicitly recommended for production | Yes for the specific role, but adds infra complexity |
| Notable dependency | None | PostgreSQL graph role requires Apache AGE extension | None beyond the product itself |

**Conflict to note:** Some secondary summaries present MongoDB and OpenSearch as equivalent unified production options alongside PostgreSQL [call-efcb1bae, call-ff664c6a], while the Railway deployment summary and step-3 evidence focus on PostgreSQL as *the* recommended production backend [call-21bdb92b, call-93b1c585]. I could not independently verify MongoDB/OpenSearch implementation details against the official docs within the evidence boundary.

---

## 4. Is PostgreSQL / Neon suitable?

### PostgreSQL — supported as suitable, with conditions

- PostgreSQL is recommended for production and can serve all four storage roles on its own [call-21bdb92b](https://railway.com/deploy/lightrag-knowledge-graph-rag-postgres-production--lightrag-postgres-graph-rag), [call-93b1c585](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md).
- Concrete storage classes exist: `PGKVStorage`, `PGVectorStorage`, `PGGraphStorage`, `PGDocStatusStorage` [call-d60bc60f](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/examples/lightrag_gemini_postgres_demo.py).
- **Graph storage dependency:** `PGGraphStorage` is built on the Apache AGE PostgreSQL extension. A stock PostgreSQL image **cannot** provide graph storage without AGE [call-a4b0432f](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/DockerDeployment.md). The referenced Docker image `gzdaniel/postgres-for-rag:pg18-age-pgvector` bundles Apache AGE + pgvector [call-a4b0432f].
- Azure documentation confirms Apache AGE adds graph (openCypher) capabilities to PostgreSQL [call-2874ab74](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/postgresql/azure-ai/generative-ai-age-overview).

### Neon — partially supported; graph role unverified

- Neon is a serverless PostgreSQL service, described as 100% Postgres-compatible, and supports the `pgvector` extension for vector similarity search [call-39908b6b](https://finance.yahoo.com/news/neon-serverless-postgres-announces-native-190800299.html), [call-b671acde](https://neon.com/docs/extensions/pgvector).
- **Critical gap:** the evidence explicitly states there are **no specific details about Neon's support for the Apache AGE extension** [call-2874ab74]. Since `PGGraphStorage` requires AGE, Neon's suitability for the **graph storage role is unverified**. Neon may be suitable for KV, vector, and document-status storage (standard Postgres + pgvector), but using it for graph storage would require confirmation that AGE can be installed/enabled on Neon, or pairing Neon with a dedicated graph database.

**Verdict:** PostgreSQL (self-managed or managed, with pgvector + Apache AGE) is a suitable, documented production setup. Neon is plausibly suitable for three of four roles but **not confirmed** for the graph role.

---

## 5. Compatibility limitations and configuration considerations

### Configuration (partially supported)
Environment variables identified for PostgreSQL configuration:
- `POSTGRES_HOST`, `POSTGRES_PORT`, `POSTGRES_USER`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD`, `POSTGRES_DATABASE`
- `LIGHTRAG_KV_STORAGE=PGKVStorage`, `LIGHTRAG_VECTOR_STORAGE=PGVectorStorage`, `LIGHTRAG_GRAPH_STORAGE=PGGraphStorage` [call-d60bc60f](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/examples/lightrag_gemini_postgres_demo.py), [call-93b1c585](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/blob/main/docs/LightRAG-API-Server.md)

### Known limitations / caveats (partially supported)
1. Default in-memory/file stores are not production-suitable [call-1fc3d299].
2. Stock PostgreSQL lacks graph storage without Apache AGE [call-a4b0432f].
3. Apache AGE support on Neon is not evidenced [call-2874ab74].
4. Official Docker image status: a feature request exists; sources do not confirm an official image has been published [call-cc9a1549](https://github.com/HKUDS/LightRAG/issues/1417).
5. Cross-check of every backend claim against official docs was not completed (step-2 limit) — `step_2:claim_5` unsupported.

---

## 6. Recommended production storage architecture (reasoned recommendation)

**Primary recommendation:** Single PostgreSQL instance (self-hosted or managed, e.g., RDS / Cloud SQL) running the `pgvector` and `apache/age` extensions, serving all four LightRAG storage roles:
- `KV_STORAGE` → `PGKVStorage`
- `VECTOR_STORAGE` → `PGVectorStorage` (pgvector)
- `GRAPH_STORAGE` → `PGGraphStorage` (Apache AGE)
- `DOC_STATUS_STORAGE` → `PGDocStatusStorage`

Configure via the environment variables above; use connection pooling, automated backups, and monitoring. Use the `gzdaniel/postgres-for-rag:pg18-age-pgvector` image pattern (or equivalent) if containerizing [call-a4b0432f].

**If Neon is required:** Use Neon for KV, vector, and document-status storage (standard Postgres + pgvector). For the graph role, either (a) confirm Apache AGE is available on Neon before committing, or (b) run a dedicated graph database (Neo4j or Memgraph) for `GRAPH_STORAGE` and keep Neon for the other three roles. Do not assume Neon supports `PGGraphStorage` without verification.

**Do not use** the default in-memory/file-persisted storage in production.

---
